The MATLAB toolbox

The Dome toolbox computes the same properties as Dome in MATLAB: states, property functions, and T–s, p–v, p–h and h–s diagrams. It runs in plain MATLAB, with nothing compiled, and gives Dome's numbers. Scripts exported from Dome use it.

Installing

MATLAB R2019b or later.

  1. Download Dome.mltbx from the download page.
  2. Open Dome.mltbx in MATLAB: double-click it, or drag it into the Command Window. MATLAB installs the toolbox.
  3. MATLAB then opens the Getting Started guide.

The Getting Started guide

dome.gettingStarted opens the guide again at any time. It is a live script with code and output for each part of the toolbox: a state from two properties (with English units), saturation and two-phase states, property functions and arrays of states, the other fluids, an ideal Rankine cycle with its T–s diagram, tables of states, updates, and the scripts Dome's MATLAB export writes. The same guide is online: Getting started with the Dome toolbox.

s1 = dome.state('water', 'p', 80, 'bar', 'T', 480, 'C')
s2 = dome.state('water', 'p', 7, 'bar', 's', s1.s);
w  = s1.h - s2.h                                   % kJ/kg
dome.plot('Ts', s1, 's', s2)

help dome lists the functions, and dome.selftest checks the installation against values computed by Dome.

Updates

Once a day, the first use of the toolbox in a MATLAB session asks whether a newer version has been published. When one has, MATLAB prints one line, for example:

Dome toolbox 0.2.0 is available (this is 0.1.0); dome.update installs it.
  • dome.update downloads the new version and installs it in place of the old one.
  • dome.version prints the version installed.
  • dome.update('off') stops the daily check, and dome.update('on') starts it again.

The check is quiet when GitHub cannot be reached.

Scripts from Dome

Publish › MATLAB script, or File › Export › MATLAB script, writes a sheet as a MATLAB script (see Publishing and exporting). With “States from the Dome MATLAB toolbox” checked, each state line becomes a call to dome.state, so the script computes again when an input changes.
